title: Fab Air-Gap POC feasibility field report
content:
Executive summary:

Field visit: customer site (Tier-1 semiconductor fab, NW US) workshop and data center tour on 2025-11-10. Purpose: assess feasibility for a 6-week air-gapped POC to validate on-device inference for fab process control use-case (real-time anomaly detection pipeline).

High-level conclusion: POC is technically feasible within current Redwood Private deployment model with the following constraints and mitigations:
- Customer has strict egress restrictions and HSM-backed key policy that require an on-prem control plane shim and manual artifact import.
- Compute footprint in the on-site cluster is limited (2x A100-s equivalent available, 1x spare). We recommend a lightweight model variant + 4-bit quantization for initial throughput targets.
- Network segmentation and jump-host procedures are stricter than typical enterprise; install runbook needs explicit step-by-step operator tasks and signed approvals.

Environment inventory (collected during tour and interviews):
- Datacenter room: private, badge-only, no external network plug-in in production racks.
- Edge cluster: 3 physical nodes (2x GPU+CPU nodes, 1x management node), Mellanox 100Gb fabric, Ceph RGW object store running as the primary artifact store.
- Control plane expectations: customer will not allow outbound connections from management node to external Redwood endpoints. All control plane actions must be proxied through an air-gapped management console and artifacts staged by their infra team.
- Identity & secrets: enterprise KMS (Thales Luna) used for KMS operations; customer requires HSM for model key sealing.
- Compliance: fab is subject to ITAR-like export controls and internal IP protection policies; any binary/artifact transfer must be logged and approved by their security compliance officer.

Customer success criteria for POC:
1) Demonstrate end-to-end inference latency <= 35 ms per inference for 512-token / 1k-timesteps equivalent workload under 50 QPS target when batching is enabled.
2) Show reproducible deployment workflow with zero external egress after artifacts are imported.
3) Validate secure key lifecycle: model keys sealed in customer's HSM, Redwood token never persistent on execution hosts.
4) Provide minimal operational dashboard: token-level cost estimate not required for POC, but latency, GPU util, and cache hit rates must be visible.

Hardware and sizing notes:
- Available: 2 x Nvidia A100 80GB-equivalent nodes (dual-socket), 1 management VM. Local Ceph provides ~120TB usable.
- Recommendation: use one node as model-serving pool (continuous-batching enabled), second node as KV-cache + fallback runtime. Keep management VM for install and API shim.
- Swap/overflow plan: if throughput exceeded, customer can allow brief burst to an approved colo in their internal network (requires extra approvals).

Network and installation constraints:
- No direct internet. Artifact provisioning must be done via signed USB image or internal artifact repo (S3-compatible Ceph RGW). We must support package signing and an offline artifact manifest for reproducible installs.
- Management node can reach internal artifact repo and HSM. Installer must support pulling from S3-compatible endpoints (not just public cloud S3) and allow custom CA bundles.
- Ports and endpoints: prepare a minimal list of ports and explicit IP ranges for the customer's firewall rule approval form.

Security and compliance requirements:
- All binaries and model weights must be SHA256-signed and checksummed. Customer will perform signature verification via their internal validation tool.
- HSM integration required for sealing model encryption keys. Redwood will provide KMS hooks; customer will supply HSM credentials and admin workflow.
- Audit logs: every install step and artifact import must be logged to a local SIEM (Splunk) with provided index. Redwood needs to provide log forwarder and schema mapping.
- No persistent outbound credentials allowed on serving hosts. Short-lived admin tokens for the installer acceptable if only present in memory and revoked after install.

Installer and packaging implications:
- We need a dedicated "airgap installer" bundle that:
  1) contains the runtime binaries (docker images or runc tarballs),
  2) offline Helm charts and manifests or equivalent k8s YAMLs for their internal k8s variant,
  3) model artifacts (quantized variants) and a signed manifest file,
  4) an installation checklist and operator prompts for manual key sealing steps.
- Preferred distribution: tarball with checksums + optional signed USB key. Must be consumable by the customer's internal artifact service (RGW).

Operational considerations (POC scope):
- Support model onboarding for a single model family (anomaly-detector-v1) and one dataset derived from their sensor stream.
- Observability: expose Prometheus metrics to their internal monitoring and provide Grafana dash templates. No external telemetry allowed.
- Upgrade flow: for POC we propose manual upgrade via new signed installer artifacts. Automated rollouts are out-of-scope for this POC due to policy.

Risk register (top items):
1) HSM / KMS integration complexity — medium/high. Mitigation: pre-work session with their security team and a dry-run using test HSM credentials.
2) Installer compatibility with their k8s distro and CNI — medium. Mitigation: capture kubelet/k8s versions and run a local no-network smoke deploy in our lab.
3) Model performance gap due to quantization trade-offs — medium. Mitigation: prepare two quantization profiles and a fallback higher-precision variant for validation.
4) Approval delays for signed USB artifact import — schedule buffer and provide incremental deliverables (docs + manifests) for early review.

Open questions / action items (owner and ETA):
- Provide list of exact k8s versions, CNI, and Ceph RGW endpoint details (Customer infra) — owner: Customer infra, ETA: 2025-11-24.
- Confirm HSM vendor and API access method (PKCS#11 vs vendor API) — owner: Customer security, ETA: 2025-11-21.
- Redwood to produce a minimal airgap installer prototype and test it in Redwood lab using Ceph RGW emulator — owner: Leah Kim, ETA: 2025-11-28.
- Prepare signed manifest and install checklist for security review — owner: Marcus Lee, ETA: 2025-11-25.

Suggested POC timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 0: pre-work (artifact signing setup, HSM test creds, env inventory confirmation).
- Weeks 1-2: airgap installer delivery + in-lab smoke test.
- Weeks 3-4: on-site install, model import, baseline inference tests.
- Weeks 5-6: performance tuning, operator handover, runbook validation, final report.

Notes to self / workshop anecdotes (informal):
- Fab ops lead insisted on 4-eyes approval for any artifact touching production racks — will need to choreograph stakeholder sign-offs.
- Customer asked about bandwidth quotas in case we need to pull large debug bundles — treat as a hard constraint, plan smaller debug bundles and remote phone sessions.
- Security team asked whether Redwood can support an absolute no-container mode (bare-binary runtime). Short answer: not today; longer-term: explore minimal runtime shim.

Immediate next steps for Redwood SE team:
1) Kick off J-2114 ticket for airgap installer prototype and attach this field report.
2) Schedule dry-run with infra in our lab; mirror customer's Ceph RGW.
3) Draft the port/IP firewall approval form and send to customer security for pre-approval.
4) Start packaging quantized model variants and sign them with CI keys (produce test artifacts for HSM verification).

References and artifacts attached to ticket:
- Prototype installer repo PR: github.com/redwood-inference/installer/pull/87
- Internal runbook template: confluence.redwood.ai/display/SE/Airgap+Runbook+Template
- Related POC notes: JIRA-ENG-1980 (previous pharma airgap) — use for installer learnings but do not reuse artifacts without re-signing.

-- end of field report --
